before.title: What Owners Are Buying
before.body: Owners buying Caption are buying an upscale select-service lifestyle hotel organized around Talk Shop, Hyatt brand standards, and World of Hyatt. They are not buying banquet depth, extended-stay kitchens, or a branded-residences stack. The bet is that a well-run commons plus Hyatt distribution can outperform a generic lifestyle box in the right walkable location. If Talk Shop cannot trade, the brand thesis does not hold.

Staff and program the commons as a business, not a brand storyboard.

Pick operators who have run all-day social F&B, not only rooms-focused select service or traditional full-service banquet culture.

before.title: Owner Watchouts
before.body:
Can Talk Shop draw hotel and neighborhood traffic as a real P&L, including off-peak days?
How does this micro-location compare with Hyatt Place, Hyatt Centric, Moxy, Aloft, and citizenM?
Is F&B labor and opening-hour coverage funded through stabilization, or will the commons be cut first?
Does the conversion/new-build budget include kitchen, acoustics, and arrival sightlines to Talk Shop?
Are World of Hyatt contribution assumptions market-specific, not corporate averages?
Is a nearby Hyatt already capturing the same guest, making Caption redundant?
Are you accidentally underwriting Hyatt Centric explorer amenities or Place-only economics?
Caption is a hotel product, not a branded-residences play—do not add residential yield into the hotel thesis
